semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious.
His saying: {تَنزِيلُ}: there are several views on it. The first: it is the khabar of «ألم», because «ألم» is meant to denote the sūra and part of the Qur'an; and «تنزيلُ» is in the sense of «مُنزَّل» ("sent down"). The sentence {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} is a ḥāl from «الكتاب», and the governing element in it is «تنزيلُ», because it is a maṣdar. And «مِنْ رَبِّ» is attached to it as well. It is also possible that it be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «فيه» because it occurs as a khabar; the governing element in it is the adverbial phrase or the notion of "being settled".
The second: «تَنْزِل» [sic] is a mubtadaʾ and «لا ريبَ فيه» is its khabar, and {مِن رَّبِّ العالمين} is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «فيه». It is then not permissible for it to be attached to «تنزيل», because the maṣdar has been predicated of and so does not govern; but one who is liberal about prepositions does not care about that. [Translator's note: the source reads «تَنْزِل» here, apparently for «تنزيلُ»; translated as written.]
The third: «تنزيلُ» is also a mubtadaʾ, «مِنْ رَبِّ» its khabar, and «لا ريبَ» a ḥāl or a parenthetical. The fourth: «لا ريب» and {مِن رَّبِّ العالمين} are two khabars of «تنزيلُ». The fifth: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, and likewise «لا ريبَ», and likewise «مِنْ ربّ», so that each sentence is independent by itself. It is also possible that they are two ḥāls from «تنزيلُ», and that «مِنْ رب» is the ḥāl and «لا ريبَ» parenthetical. The beginning of al-Baqara is a guide to this; I repeated it only to refresh it.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed {مِن رَّبِّ العالمين} to be attached to «تنزيل», saying: "by fronting and postponing." The Shaykh rejected it: if we say {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} is parenthetical, there is no fronting and postponing; indeed, had it been postponed it would not be parenthetical. He also allowed that it be attached to «لا ريبَ», that is, "there is no doubt about it from the side of the Lord of the worlds"; and if doubt occurred among the disbelievers, that is not taken into account.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ}: it is the disconnected «أم», and the iḍrāb (turning away) is a transition, not a refutation.
His saying: {بَلْ هُوَ الحق}: a second iḍrāb. Had it been said that it is an iḍrāb of refutation of «افتراه» alone, it would have been correct; and on this it is said: every iḍrāb in the Qur'an is a transition except this one, for it may be a refutation, because it refutes their statement, that is, "it is not, as they said, a fabrication; rather it is the truth". In al-Zamakhsharī's discourse is something that guides to this, for he said: "The pronoun in «فيه» returns to the content of the sentence, as if it were said: there is no doubt about that, that is, about its being from the Lord of the worlds. In support of its soundness is His saying {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ: افتراه}, because their statement 'this is fabricated' is a denial that it is from the Lord of the worlds; and likewise His saying {بَلْ هُوَ الحق مِن رَّبِّكَ} contains the affirmation that it is from Allah. This is a sound, firm style."
His saying: «مِنْ ربِّك»: a ḥāl from «الحقّ»; its governing element is omitted by the rule, and it is also the governing element of «لِتُنْذِرَ». The governing element of «لتنذر» may also be another, that is, "He sent it down so that you may warn".
His saying: {قَوْماً مَّآ أَتَاهُم}: the apparent view is that the second object of the warning is omitted, and «قوماً» is the first, the implied form being "so that you may warn a people of the punishment"; and «ما أتاهم» is a negated sentence in the position of accusative as an adjective of «قوماً». He means: those in the interval between ʿĪsā and Muḥammad, peace be upon them. Al-Zamakhsharī made it like His saying {لِتُنذِرَ قَوْماً مَّآ أُنذِرَ آبَآؤُهُمْ} [Yā Sīn: 6]. On this, «مِنْ نذير» is the fāʿil of «أتاهم», and «مِنْ» is redundant in it, and «مِنْ قبلِك» is an adjective of «نذير». It is also possible that «مِنْ قبلك» be attached to «أتاهم».
The Shaykh allowed «ما» to be relative in both places, and the implied form is: "so that you may warn a people of the punishment that came to them from a warner before you." «مِنْ نذير» is attached to «أتاهم», that is, "it came to them on the tongue of a warner before you"; likewise {لِتُنذِرَ قَوْماً مَّآ أُنذِرَ آبَآؤُهُمْ} [Yā Sīn: 6], that is, "the punishment with which their fathers were warned". So «ما» is an object in both places, and «لِتُنْذرَ» governs two objects. The Exalted said: {فَقُلْ أَنذَرْتُكُمْ صَاعِقَةً} [Fuṣṣilat: 13]. This view runs along the apparent sense of the Qur'an. The Exalted said: {وَإِن مِّنْ أُمَّةٍ إِلاَّ خَلاَ فِيهَا نَذِيرٌ} [Fāṭir: 24] and {أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا جَآءَنَا مِن بَشِيرٍ وَلاَ نَذِيرٍ فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَشِيرٌ وَنَذِيرٌ} [al-Māʾida: 19]. I say: what he said is apparent.
It appears that in the other verse there is another analysis: that «ما» is a maṣdar particle, its implied form being "so that you may warn a people with a warning like the warning of their fathers", because all the messengers agree on the word of truth.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ يَعْرُجُ}: the majority read it active. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it passive. The origin is «يُعْرَجُ به», then the preposition was omitted so the pronoun became nominative and latent. It is anomalous (shādhdh), and is suited to justify the like of it.
His saying: «مِمَّا تَعُدُّون»: the majority read it in the second person. Al-Ḥasan, al-Sulamī, Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read it in the third person. This prepositional phrase is an adjective of «أَلْف» or of «سَنة».

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {ذلك عَالِمُ}: the majority read «عالمُ», «العزيز» and «الرحيم» in the nominative, with «ذلك» as a mubtadaʾ and «عالمُ» its khabar, and «العزيز الرحيم» two khabars or two adjectives; or «العزيز الرحيم» is a mubtadaʾ with its adjective and «الذي أَحْسَنَ» its khabar; or «العزيزُ الرحيم» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read all three in the genitive. Its analysis, with its difficulty, is that «ذلك» points to the managed affair (al-amr al-mudabbar) and is the fāʿil of «يَعْرُجُ», and the three attributes are a badal for the pronoun in «إليه», as if it were said: "then the managed affair ascends to Him, the Knower of the unseen", that is, to the Knower of the unseen.
Abū Zayd read «عالمُ» in the nominative and «العزيزِ الرحيمِ» in the genitive, so that «ذلك عالمُ» is mubtadaʾ and khabar, and «العزيزِ الرحيمِ» are two badals from the hāʾ in «إليه» as well, with the sentence between them parenthetical.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {الذي أَحْسَنَ}: it may follow what precedes it in both the nominative and genitive readings; it may be another khabar; it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ; and it may be accusative for praise.
His saying: «خَلَقَه»: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with sukūn on the lām («خَلْقَه»). The others read it with fatḥa. As for the first, it has several analyses. The first: «خَلْقَه» is a badal al-ishtimāl from «كلَّ شيء», and the pronoun returns to «كل شيء». This is the famous, current view. The second: it is a badal al-kull min al-kull (total substitute), and the pronoun on this returns to the Creator the Exalted. The meaning of «أحسن» is «حَسَّن» ("made good"), because there is nothing He created except that it is arranged as wisdom requires, so all creatures are good. The third: «كلَّ شيءٍ» is the first object and «خَلْقَه» the second, with «أحسَنَ» taking on the sense of "gave" and "inspired". Mujāhid said: "He gave every kind its shape." The meaning: He created every thing in its form that He assigned to it. The fourth: «كلَّ شيء» is the second object, fronted, and «خَلْقَه» the first object, postponed, with «أَحْسَنَ» taking on the sense of "inspired" and "made known". Al-Farrāʾ said: "He inspired everything with its creation in what they need, so He made them know that." I say: Abū al-Baqāʾ made «أحسنَ» take the sense of "made known", and parsed it as above, except that the pronoun must be made for Allah the Exalted, and «الخَلْق» made in the sense of «المَخْلوق», that is, "He made His creatures know everything they need", so the meaning comes back to the meaning of His saying {أعطى كُلَّ شَيءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هدى} [Ṭā Hā: 50].
The fifth: the hāʾ returns [to Allah the Exalted] and «خَلْقَه» is accusative as a maṣdar emphasizing the content of the sentence, like His saying {صُنْعَ الله} [al-Naml: 88]; this is Sībawayh's position, that is, "He created it a creation". It was given preference over badal al-ishtimāl because it contains the annexation of the maṣdar to its agent, which is more frequent than its annexation to the object; and because it is more eloquent as a favour: for when He says {أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ} it is more eloquent than «أَحْسَنَ خَلْقَ كلِّ شيء» ("made good the creation of everything"), since the act of creating, which is the attempt, may be good while the thing itself is not good; whereas when He says "He made everything good", it implies that everything He created is good, in the sense that He placed everything in its proper place.
As for the second reading, «خَلَقَ» in it is a past verb, and the sentence is an adjective of the muḍāf or the muḍāf ilayhi, so it is accusative or genitive in position.
His saying: «وَبَدَأ»: the majority read it with the hamza. Al-Zuhrī read «بدا» with a pure alif, which departs from the rule of its softening, since the rule is the intermediate pronunciation (bayna bayna). Although al-Akhfash reported «قَرَيْتُ», the Shaykh allowed it to be from the dialect of the Anṣār. They say «بَدِي» for «بدأ», with kasra on the dāl and a yāʾ after it, as in the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa al-Anṣārī:
3669 - بسمِ الإِلهِ وبه بَدِيْنا ... ولو عَبَدْنا غيرَه شَقِيْنا
(In the name of the Deity and by Him we began; had we worshipped other than Him we would have been wretched.)
He said: "And Ṭayyiʾ say for «بقي», «بَقَا»." He said: "So it is possible that al-Zuhrī's reading is from this dialect, its origin being «بَدِي», then it became «بدا»." I say: then the reading is compounded from two dialects.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ}: this is an iltifāt from the singular third-person pronoun in His saying «نَسْلَه» and on, to the address of a group.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {أَإِذَا ضَلَلْنَا}: the disagreement of the reciters about the two interrogatives was discussed in Sūrat al-Raʿd. The governing element of «إذا» is omitted, its implied form being "we will be raised" or "we will be brought out", because «خَلْقٍ جديد» points to it. «خَلْق جديد» cannot govern it, because what comes after «إنَّ» and the interrogative does not govern what precedes them. The apodosis of «إذا» is omitted if you take it as conditional.
The majority read «ضَلَلْنا» with dotted ḍād and fatḥa on the lām in the sense of "we disappeared and were lost", from their saying «ضَلَّ اللبنُ في الماء» ("the milk was lost in the water"). It was also said: "we were hidden". Al-Nābigha said:
3670 - فآبَ مُضِلُّوه بعينٍ جَلِيَّة ... وغُوْدِر بالجَوْلانِ حَزْمٌ ونائِلُ
(Those who buried him returned with clear eyes, and prudence and generosity were left behind in al-Jawlān.)
The imperfect of this is «يَضِلُّ» with kasra on the ʿayn, and it is frequent. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū Rajāʾ read it with kasra on the lām, which is the dialect of al-ʿĀliya; the imperfect of this is «يَضَلُّ» with fatḥa. ʿAlī and Abū Ḥaywa read «ضُلِّلْنا» with ḍamma on the ḍād and a doubled kasra-vowelled lām, from «ضَلَّلَه» with doubling.
ʿAlī also, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and Abān ibn Saʿīd read «صَلَلْنا» with undotted ṣād and fatḥa on the lām. And from al-Ḥasan also «صَلِلْنا» with kasra on the ṣād. They are two dialects. It is said «صَلَّ اللحمُ يَصِلُّ» and «يَصَلُّ» with fatḥa or kasra of the ṣād, because the past occurs with fatḥa or kasra on the ʿayn. The meaning of «صَلَّ اللحمُ»: it stank and its smell changed. It is also said «أَصَلَّ» with an alif. He said:
3671 - تُلَجْلِجُ مُضْغَةً فيها أَنِيْضٌ ... أَصَلَّتْ، فَهْيَ تحت الكَشْحِ داءُ
(She rolls a morsel in which there is half-cooked [meat]; it has turned foul, so beneath the flank it is a sickness.)
Al-Naḥḥās said: "We do not know «صَلِلْنا» in the language, but it is said «صَلَّ اللحمُ» and «أصلَّ», and «خَمَّ» and «أَخَمَّ»." Others than Abū Jaʿfar have known it.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {تُرْجَعُونَ}: the majority read it passive. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it active.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَلَوْ ترى}: there are two views on this «لو». The first: it is for what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else. Al-Zamakhsharī expressed it as "impossibility because of impossibility", and the Shaykh disputed him on that. Its thorough treatment has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. On this, its apodosis is omitted, that is, "you would have seen a dreadful matter". The second: it is for wishing. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "as if it were said: «وَلَيْتَكَ ترى»." When it is for wishing there is disagreement: does it require an apodosis or not? The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's supposition here is that it has none. The Shaykh said: "The sound view is that it has an apodosis." And he recited the verse of the poet:
3672 - فلو نُبِشَ المقابرُ عن كُلَيْبٍ ... فَيُخبِرَ بالذَّنائبِ أيُّ زِيْرِ
بيومِ الشَّعْثَمَيْنِ لَقَرَّ عيناً ... وكيف لِقاءُ مَنْ تحتَ القُبورِ
(If the graves were dug up for Kulayb, and he were told, by the dhanāʾib, what kind of woman-chaser [Zīr was] on the day of the two Shaʿthams, his eye would be cooled; but how can one under the graves be met?)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لو» comes in the sense of wishing, as you say «لو تأتيني فتحدثَني» just as you say «ليتك تأتيني فتحدثني»." Ibn Mālik said: "If he means by it omission, that is, «وَدِدْتُ لو تأتيني فتحدثَني» ('I wish you would come to me and talk to me'), it is correct; but if he means that it is coined for it, it is not correct; for if it were coined for it, it would not be combined with it, just as «ليت» is not combined with «أتمنى», nor «لعلَّ» with «أترجَّى», nor «إلاَّ» with «أَسْتَثْني». It is permissible to combine «لو» with «أتمنى»: you say «تمنَّيْتُ لو فعلتُ كذا» ('I wished I had done such-and-such')." Is the addressee the Prophet ﷺ or another? There is disagreement. «إذ» is in its usual sense of the past, because «لو» turns the imperfect to the past. It was put in the past here for the certainty of its occurrence, like {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1]. Abū al-Baqāʾ made it one of the cases where «إذ» stands in the place of «إذا», and there is no need for it.
His saying: «ناكِسُو»: the majority read it as an active participle annexed to its object for lightness. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «نَكَسُوا» as a past verb, with «رؤوسَهم» as a direct object.
His saying: «ربَّنا»: on the implication of "saying", and it is a ḥāl, that is, "saying that". Al-Zamakhsharī supposed "they cry for help by their saying", but the implication of "saying" is more frequent.
His saying: «أَبْصَرْنا وسَمِعْنا»: the object may be supposed, that is, "we have seen what we used to deny, and heard what we used to reject"; or it may not be supposed, that is, "we have become seeing and hearing".
His saying: «صالحاً»: it may be a direct object, or an adjective of a maṣdar.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {لِقَآءَ يَوْمِكُمْ}: several views are possible in this verse. The first: it is a case of tanāzuʿ (competition), because «ذُوقوا» requires «لقاءَ يومِكم» and «نَسِيْتُمْ» requires it too, that is, "taste the punishment of the meeting of this your Day because you forgot the punishment of the meeting of this your Day"; it is an instance of giving effect to the second according to the Basrans, and to the first according to the Kufans. The first is sounder because of omission from the first; for had the first been given effect, a pronoun would be supplied in the second. The second: the object of «ذُوْقوا» is omitted, that is, "taste the punishment because of your forgetting the meeting of your Day", and «هذا» in these two analyses is an adjective of «يومِكم». The third: the object of «ذوقوا» is «هذا», the pointer referring to the punishment, and the bāʾ is also causal, that is, "so taste this punishment because of your forgetting the meeting of your Day". The apparent sense resists this.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {تتجافى}: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl, and likewise «يَدْعُون»; if «يَدْعُون» is made a ḥāl it may be a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «جُنوبُهم», because the muḍāf is a part. «التجافي» is rising, by which is expressed leaving sleep. Ibn Rawāḥa said:
3673 - نبيٌّ يُجافي جَنْبُه عن فراشِه ... إذا اسْتَثْقَلَتْ بالمشركين المضاجعُ
(A prophet whose side keeps away from his bed when the beds weigh heavy on the polytheists.)
And «خَوْفاً وطَمَعاً»: either an object of purpose, or two ḥāls, or two maṣdars of an implied governing verb.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: «أُخْفِيَ»: Ḥamza read «أُخْفِيْ» as an imperfect verb attributed to the first-person pronoun, hence its yāʾ is sukūn-vowelled because it is nominative [indicative]. The reading of Ibn Masʿūd «ما نُخْفي» with the nūn of majesty supports it. The others read «أُخْفِيَ» as a passive past, hence its yāʾ takes fatḥa. Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb read «أَخْفى» as an active past, the agent being Allah the Exalted, and the reading of al-Aʿmash «ما أَخْفَيْتُ», attributed to the speaker, supports it. ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd], Abū al-Dardāʾ and Abū Hurayra read «مِّن قُرَّاتِ أَعْيُنٍ» in the plural with alif and tāʾ. And «ما» may be relative, that is, "we do not know what Allah has hidden". In the ḥadīth: "What no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has not occurred to the heart of any human." It may also be interrogative, suspending «تَعْلَمُ»; if «تعلم» governs two objects, it fills the place of both, or of one, if one. And «جزاءً» is an object of purpose, or a maṣdar emphasizing the meaning of the sentence before it. When «ما» is interrogative, then in the reading of the one who read what follows it as a past verb, it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the verb after it the khabar; and in the reading of the one who read it as an imperfect, it is a fronted object, and «مِنْ قُرَّة» is a ḥāl from «ما».

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {لاَّ يَسْتَوُونَ}: resumptive. It has been reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he used to deliberately pause at His saying «فاسقاً» and then begin «لا يَسْتوون».

semin-durr:19-19.t: Ṭalḥa read «جَنَّةُ المَأْوى» in the singular. The majority read it in the plural. Abū Ḥaywa read «نُزْلاً» with ḍamma and sukūn, and its thorough treatment has preceded at the end of Āl ʿImrān.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {الذي كُنتُمْ بِهِ}: an adjective of «عذابَ». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be an adjective of «النار», saying: it was put in the masculine in the sense of «الجحيم» and «الحريق».

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ أَعْرَضَ}: this [«ثم»] is for the distance between the two ranks in meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī likened it to his saying:
367 - 4- وما يَكْشِفُ الغَمَّاءَ إلاَّ ابنُ حُرَّةٍ ... يَرَى غَمَراتِ الموتِ ثم يَزورُها
(None removes the distress except a free-born man, who sees the depths of death and then visits them.)
[Translator's note: the verse number is garbled in the source ("367 - 4-"), probably 3674.] He said: "He deemed it remote that he would visit the depths of death after having seen them, known them and learned of their severity."

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {فِي مِرْيَةٍ}: al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma, and it is a dialect.
His saying: «مِنْ لقائِه»: regarding the hāʾ there are several views. The first: it returns to Mūsā, and the maṣdar is annexed to its object, that is, "from your meeting Mūsā on the night of the Isrāʾ". Al-Mubarrad tested al-Zajjāj on this question and he answered him with what has been mentioned. The second: the pronoun returns to the Book. Then the annexation may be to the agent, that is, "from the Book's meeting Mūsā", or to the object, that is, "from Mūsā's meeting the Book", because the meeting can be attributed to either of them. The third: it returns to the Book, with an omitted muḍāf, that is, "from meeting the like of the Book of Mūsā". The fourth: it returns to the Angel of Death, because of the earlier mention of him. The fifth: it returns to the return, understood from "return" in His saying {إلى رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ}, that is, "do not be in doubt about the meeting of the return". The sixth: it returns to what is understood from the context of the discourse, namely the trial and testing with which Mūsā was afflicted; so said al-Ḥasan, that is, "you must meet what Mūsā met from his people". These are remote views; I mentioned them to point out their weakness. The most apparent: the pronoun is either for Mūsā or for the Book, that is, "do not doubt that Mūsā met the Book and that it was sent down to him".

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {لَمَّا [صَبَرُواْ]}: the two brothers read it with kasra on the lām and a lightened mīm, so that it is the lām of genitive, and «ما» is a maṣdar particle. The prepositional phrase is attached to the making, that is, "We made them so because of their patience and their certainty". The others read it with fatḥa and a doubled mīm. It is the «لمَّا» that requires an apodosis. The two views of Sībawayh and al-Fārisī about it have preceded.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {يُبْصِرُونَ}: the majority read it in the third person; Ibn Masʿūd in the second person as an iltifāt.
«الجُرْز» was also read with sukūn on the rāʾ. It was discussed at the beginning of al-Kahf.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ الفتح}: accusative by «لا يَنْفَعُ», and «لا» does not prevent that. Positions about it have preceded.

semin-durr:30-30.t: His saying: {مُّنتَظِرُونَ}: the majority read it with kasra on the ẓāʾ, an active participle. The object of «انتظِرْ» and of «منتظرون» is omitted, that is, "wait for what will befall them; they are waiting, by their own claim, for what will befall you". Al-Yamānī read «مُنْتَظَرُون» as a passive participle.
